question: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" total domestic gross by August 31?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to how much "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" box office will gross domestically by August 31, 2026. The "Daily Box Office Performance" figures found on the "Box Office" tab on this movie's The Numbers (https://www.the-numbers.com/) page will be used to resolve this market once the values for all dates between opening (July 31, 2026) and August 31, 2026 are final (i.e., not studio estimates).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Please note, this market will resolve according to the The Numbers figures provided under Box Office Performance until and including August 31, 2026, regardless of whether domestic refers to only the USA, or to USA and Canada, etc.

If there is ambiguity as to whether the resolution source's figures are final, this market will remain open until both https://www.boxofficemojo.com/ and https://www.the-numbers.com/ have confirmed their finalized figures.

If there is no final data available by September 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.
research:
I've left out every source dated after 2026-08-16. The Numbers page showed daily figures that run past the cutoff, so I only report its numbers through Aug 15.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-08-15 (last day reported by Aug 16): The Numbers' daily table shows a cumulative domestic gross of **$763.9M** through Saturday Aug 15. Daily grosses: Jul 31, $169.8M (the $72M Jul 30 previews appear as a separate line); Aug 1, $101.5M; Aug 2, $88.7M; second weekend (Aug 7-9) $42.8M / $56.7M / $44.8M; Aug 10-13 weekdays $16.7M / $20.0M / $13.5M / $11.3M; Aug 14, $19.0M; Aug 15, $29.1M. [The Numbers](https://www.the-numbers.com/movie/Spider-Man-Brand-New-Day-(2026)#tab=box-office)
- 2026-08-16: The Sunday estimate put the cumulative total through day 17 at about **$785.8M**. [Plugged In](https://www.pluggedin.com/?p=42183)

## 2. Current status
- Every bracket below $700M is already settled in practice, since the total passed $700M on Aug 12. As of Aug 16 the total is about $786M, so the answer will be either **800-900m** or **900m+**. The film reaches $800M with about $14M more, which a single weekday-plus-weekend stretch would cover.
- What's still open: to reach $900M by Aug 31, it needs about **$114M more over the 15 days from Aug 17 to Aug 31**. That window has two full weekends (Aug 21-23 and Aug 28-30) plus Monday Aug 31. Note that Aug 31 is not a holiday: Labor Day is Sep 7.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-16: The third weekend came in at about $70M (Deadline's early projection was $65M, with $19M on Friday). That is the second-best third weekend ever, behind The Force Awakens ($90.2M) and ahead of both Avatar films. The film moved to No. 4 on the all-time domestic chart. [Rotten Tomatoes](https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/weekend-box-office-spider-man-brand-new-day-week-3/); [Screen Daily](https://www.screendaily.com/news/spider-man-brand-new-day-vaults-to-number-four-in-all-time-us-box-office-rankings/5219433.article); [ComicBookMovie](https://comicbookmovie.com/spider_man/spider_man-brand-new-day/spider-man-brand-new-day-eyes-65m-third-weekend-the-end-of-oak-street-struggles-with-so-so-cinemascore-a229372)
- 2026-08-16: The new competitor, The End of Oak Street, struggled and got a so-so CinemaScore. [ComicBookMovie](https://comicbookmovie.com/spider_man/spider_man-brand-new-day/spider-man-brand-new-day-eyes-65m-third-weekend-the-end-of-oak-street-struggles-with-so-so-cinemascore-a229372)
- 2026-08-09: The second weekend was about $145M (on The Numbers, Aug 7-9 adds up to $144.3M). [BoxofficePro](https://www.boxofficepro.com/weekend-box-office-spider-man-brand-new-day-takes-145m-in-sophomore-frame/)
- 2026-08-03: Monday actuals put the opening at $360M, a record above Endgame's $357.1M. [THR](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/spider-man-brand-new-day-opening-record-endgame-box-office-1236662986/); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/02/spider-man-brand-new-day-box-office-355-million-domestic-opening.html)

## 4. Base rates
These are from my own memory and approximate, so please verify them.
- Weekend-to-weekend drops: about -60% from weekend 1 to 2, then about -51% from weekend 2 to 3. Weekdays in the week of Aug 10-13 ran $11-20M a day.
- Avengers: Endgame (2019) had about $723.5M by day 17 and roughly $805M by day 31-32, a gain of about $80M.
- The Force Awakens (2015) had about $742M by day 17 and about $860M by day 31, a gain of about $118M. That run was boosted by the holidays.
- Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) had about $613M by day 17 and about $703M by day 31, a gain of about $90M.
- A rough path: a weekend 4 down 40-45% from $70M would be about $39-42M, and a weekend 5 down another 40-45% would be about $22-25M. Summer weekdays early in that stretch would be about $5-10M a day, falling to $3-5M the following week. That adds up to roughly $95-125M for Aug 17-31, which puts $900M (needing $114M) close to the middle of the plausible range.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-04: Polymarket gave the film a reported 73% chance of passing $900M domestic by the end of August. [Action Network](https://www.actionnetwork.com/entertainment/spider-man-brand-new-day-how-much-money-will-it-make) (I couldn't load the page itself; this comes from a search summary.)
- About 2026-08-16: A Polyguana snapshot reportedly priced the 900m+ bracket at about 32% Yes (68% No), a sharp fall after the third weekend. I couldn't verify this directly because the page redirects to X. [Polyguana](https://polyguana.com/market/2966557); [Polymarket mirror](https://polymarkets.co.il/en/market/spider-man-brand-new-day-total-domestic-gross-by-august-31-20260716181307512/)
- I didn't find matching markets on Kalshi or Manifold.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-17: Monday actuals will confirm or revise the $785.8M estimate.
- Aug 21-23 (weekend 4): Insidious 6 opens, and Paw Patrol and Oak Street are holdovers. This weekend's drop is the main signal for whether $900M is reachable.
- Late August: more schools go back, which usually weakens weekday grosses.
- Aug 28-30 (weekend 5) and Monday Aug 31: these are the last days that count. Labor Day weekend (Sep 4-7) falls outside the window.
- Any premium-format (PLF/IMAX) screens lost to new releases would also hurt.
